_about: Intentional, audited divergences from the verbatim v1 content. The reference sections (src/content/sections/*.html) and the live calculator subsystem (src/ui/calculators-live.mjs) are generated from main:v1/flowchart.html and are held byte-identical to it by gates 9 and 10, so a figure that goes stale there cannot be fixed by editing those files. Each entry below is applied by tools/build-v2.mjs on top of the verbatim text at build time; tools/verify-corrections.mjs (gate 13) proves every 'find' still matches the verbatim source exactly 'count' times, so a v1 change or a silent drift fails the build. Tokens in 'replace': {{fig:key}} -> the figure's display string, {{figval:key}} -> its raw number. Hand-typed derived numbers carry the derivation in 'reason'. Every entry names the audit claim it corrects and the primary source read on 'verified'.

corrections.find: The 2026 limit is $5,000 per household (regardless of filing status; not per parent)
corrections.replace: The 2026 limit is {{fig:limit_dcfsa}} per household ({{fig:limit_dcfsa_mfs}} if married filing separately; not per parent)
corrections.reason: P.L. 119-21 §70404 raised the §129(a)(2)(A) exclusion from $5,000 ($2,500 MFS) to $7,500 ($3,750 MFS) for taxable years beginning after 2025-12-31; the v1 text predates it. 'Regardless of filing status' was also wrong for married filing separately.

corrections.find: a fully-funded DCFSA saves roughly $1,830/year in taxes
corrections.replace: a fully-funded DCFSA saves roughly $2,750/year in taxes
corrections.source: Derived from limit_dcfsa (figures.json) and the rates stated in the same sentence

corrections.reason: The calculator's default and ceiling were the old limit; a user could not enter the 2026 amount.
Fallback default of the DCFSA calculator tracks the corrected input default (COR-003).
